1	# @magpie-community/opencode-zcode-auth
2	
3	Signs in to Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan, or BigModel's (智谱). It does this the
4	way [ZCode](https://zcode.z.ai) does, and serves the plan's GLM models
5	over Anthropic's Messages API. Provider id: `zcode`.
6	
7	## Signing in
8	
9	- **ZCode: Z.ai GLM Coding Plan** and **ZCode: BigModel (智谱) GLM Coding Plan**
10	  - zcode.z.ai opens a sign-in flow, and the browser signs in to Z.ai or to
11	    BigModel. The plugin polls the flow until it is done, so there is
12	    nothing to paste.
13	  - With that sign-in it takes the key named `zcode-api-key` from the
14	    account's default project, or makes it if it isn't there, as ZCode does.
15	    Requests go to `api.z.ai/api/anthropic` or
16	    `open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic`.
17	  - If the account has no plan of its own, it looks for a seat on a team's
18	    plan and uses that team project's `zcode-team-api-key`.
19	  - Failing both, it uses ZCode's free **Start Plan**, served by zcode.z.ai
20	    with ZCode's session token.
21	  - zcode.z.ai serves the Start Plan only to requests that look like the
22	    ZCode client's own, and refuses others with HTTP 405 "request has been
23	    blocked due to unusual activity". So a Start Plan request goes as
24	    ZCode's does: ZCode's headers, ZCode's three system blocks with the
25	    agent's system prompt at the end of the third (a fourth block is
26	    refused, #343), the day in a `<system-reminder>` turn before the agent's
27	    turns, and the sign-in's device id in `metadata.user_id`. GLM Coding
28	    Plan and team requests go as the agent sent them. One it still turns
29	    away (a 405, the block page or code 3012) comes back with what to do
30	    about it, as magpie's built-in said: "ZCode's Start Plan still turned
31	    this request away, though magpie sends it as the ZCode app does; …
32	    Use an account with a GLM Coding Plan, or add another provider to this
33	    group".
34	  - The Start Plan's token can't be refreshed. When it runs out, sign in
35	    again.
36	- **ZCode: a team's GLM Coding Plan**
37	  - For an account with a plan of its own and a seat on a team's plan
38	    (#285). The sign-ins above take the account's own plan, as ZCode does
39	    by default; this one asks which site, signs in the same way, and
40	    takes the team seat's `zcode-team-api-key`, as ZCode does when its
41	    plan picker is switched to the team's plan.
42	  - It is kept as an account of its own, named `<email> (team)`, beside
43	    the account's own plan, so both can be used.
44	  - With no seat on a team's plan, it says so and signs in to nothing.
45	- **ZCode app's sign-in**
46	  - Uses the account the ZCode app on this computer is signed in to. For
47	    every request it reads ZCode's own credentials (`~/.zcode/v2`), so it
48	    follows ZCode as it signs in again, renews its session or switches to a
49	    team's plan, but only while ZCode is signed in to that same account.
50	    Once ZCode signs out, or signs in to another account, the sign-in uses
51	    what it saved when it was added; when that session has run out, it
52	    asks to be signed in again. It never sends one account's requests with
53	    another's credentials: to use both, add the app's sign-in once for each.
54	- **GLM Coding Plan API key**
55	  - Paste a key (`<id>.<secret>`) and say which site it is from.
56	
57	## Where the sign-in is kept
58	
59	In OpenCode's `auth.json` (magpie: `plugin-auth.json`), under `zcode`:
60	
61	- **The browser sign-ins** are kept as an `oauth` entry:
62	  - `access` is the key.
63	  - `refresh` is JSON holding the site, the endpoint, the key, ZCode's
64	    token, the team project, the plan and a device id of this plugin's own.
65	- **A pasted key** is kept as an `api` entry, with the site in `metadata`.
66	
67	The plugin never writes ZCode's own credential store. It reads it only for
68	the ZCode app's sign-in (`refresh` then holds `"source": "zcode"`).
69	
70	## How requests are routed
71	
72	Before each request, the plugin checks which plan the account is on, and
73	asks again every 10 minutes:
74	
75	- If the key's account has a GLM Coding Plan
76	  (`/api/biz/subscription/list`), its requests go to that plan. A model
77	  the account's gift plans also serve is listed again as
78	  `<model>-Trial`; asking that entry spends the gift (see below).
79	- Otherwise they go to the gift plans.
80	
81	Every request carries the key as both `x-api-key` and
82	`Authorization: Bearer`.
83	
84	**The gift's trial entries.** An account with a GLM Coding Plan can
85	also hold gift plans from ZCode activities, ones that expire on a fixed
86	date. Their allowance would lapse unused if every request went to the
87	coding plan, so the plugin reads the gift's balance (per the sign-in's
88	session, kept for 10 minutes) and lists every model a live bucket
89	serves again as `<model>-Trial`, named in the catalog's spelling
90	(GLM-5.3-Flash-Trial). Asking a trial entry sends the model to the
91	gift, dressed as ZCode's own; asking the plain model spends the coding
92	plan — the choice is the user's. A bucket is judged spent only by its
93	`remaining_units` — a missing one is unknown, not spent. A trial entry
94	whose bucket is spent or blocked answers 429 without touching the
95	coding plan; when the gift answers a trial entry with a quota error
96	(code 1113 "Insufficient balance or no resource package", code 1005
97	"exceed quota limit", which it can answer inside an HTTP 200) that too
98	becomes a 429 and keeps the entry off for a minute. Any other gift
99	answer (its 405, its 401, its 5xx) goes on as it came: the user picked
100	the gift, so the coding plan is not spent behind their back. Every 429
101	counts as spent, Z.ai's 1302/1303 rate limits among them. A stream's
102	body is never read or buffered on the way.
103	
104	## The usage card
105	
106	An account with both plans shows both allowances: the coding plan's
107	windows first, then the gift's buckets, each with its own name, models
108	and end. The card's plan and term stay the coding plan's. A gift read
109	that fails leaves just the coding card — magpie hides a card's windows
110	behind an error, so a gift hiccup must not black out a working Coding
111	Plan. A gift that goes out of date while requests use it simply stops
112	showing.
113	
114	**Resets.** A GLM Coding Plan of the account's own, and a team seat,
115	show the resets the vendor's usage page lists
116	(`/api/biz/customer-package-reset/list`, `targetType=PERSONAL` with the
117	plan's key, `TEAM` with the team's sign-in): how many of the five hours
118	and of the week are still available, and when each runs out, soonest
119	first. A team's are marked a team's. They are only read; a reset is
120	spent on the vendor's own page. A list that can't be read, or has none
121	left, shows no count.
122	
123	**Gift plans ZCode holds but has not granted.** ZCode hands out one-off
124	trust-build / gift plans (a day's ZCode Trust Build, say) that are not
125	on the account until the ZCode app claims them. The plugin reads the
126	app's own list of them (`GET /api/v1/zcode-plan/billing/preview`) with
127	the card and names them there — the window is named "Gift plans to
128	claim in the ZCode app" and the display shows "1 · ZCode Trust Build"
129	— set aside, so the line stops nothing and routing, usage caps and the
130	menu bar pass it over. The name is a fixed sentence magpie can
131	translate; the count and the plan's own name are the display. The plugin never claims one: the claim needs the
132	Aliyun captcha attestation only the app's renderer can make. A preview
133	that fails, or lists nothing, adds no line at all, and a card that is an
134	error keeps its error. Claim the plan in the ZCode app (open it once);
135	the next read shows it as an ordinary gift bucket.
136	
137	## Models
138	
139	The models are the ones ZCode offers for the account's plan. They come
140	from ZCode's provider config: the release zcode.z.ai names, or an
141	installed ZCode's copy if that one is newer. The list is kept for 10
142	minutes. When the config can't be read, the plugin falls back to this list:
143	
144	| Model | Context | Output | Efforts |
145	|---|---|---|---|
146	| GLM-5.3 | 1M | 128K | low, high, max |
147	| GLM-5.3-Flash | 1M | 128K | low, high, max |
148	| GLM-5.2 | 1M | 128K | none, high, max |
149	| GLM-5-Turbo | 200K | 64K | none, high |
150	
151	The Start Plan's config has all of these except GLM-5.3. An account
152	with no GLM Coding Plan also lists every model its gift plans serve under
153	the model's own name, as ZCode does (the Start Plan's GLM-5.3 bucket makes
154	GLM-5.3 a model), since all of its requests go to the gift anyway.
155	
156	A gift plan's models appear again as `<model>-Trial` entries, so a
157	request can spend the gift's quota on purpose. A trial entry is listed
158	while any live bucket serves its model, spent buckets included (a spent
159	entry answers 429 rather than vanishing mid-session).
160	
161	Two plans can give one model (ZCode Trust Build and the Start Plan both
162	give GLM-5.3-Flash). The server picks the bucket, so the usage card
163	counts the model on its live bucket, the least used, and sets a spent
164	sibling aside. A spent sibling never makes the model, or the account,
165	look used up while another bucket still has quota.

On a Start Plan (gift-only, no GLM Coding Plan) account, every request that carries a non-empty `system` is now refused by `zcode.z.ai` with `405 {"code":3012,"msg":"request has been blocked due to unusual activity."}`. The same account, model and route succeed when `system` is absent. `dress()` appends the agent's own system text as a 4th (and 5th) block after ZCode's three; the gateway accepts 2–3 blocks, so the Start Plan route dies for every coding agent — all of them send a system prompt.

**Environment**

- Windows 10.0.26300 x64, magpie 0.1.1339, `@magpie-community/opencode-zcode-auth` 0.1.20 (npm latest)
- Account: Start Plan only. `billing/balance` answers 200; the GLM-5.3 daily bucket had ~2.97M tokens left at the time.
- Route: `POST https://zcode.z.ai/api/v1/zcode-plan/anthropic/v1/messages`, model `GLM-5.3` (same for `GLM-5.3-Flash`).

**Repro through magpie**

POST `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/messages` with `{"model":"zcode/GLM-5.3","max_tokens":8,"messages":[...]}`:

- no `system` → 200
- `"system": "x"` → 405 in ~70 ms
- `system` of any size (500 B – 32 KB) → 405
- 32 KB of text in the user message instead → 200
- `tools`, assistant history, content blocks → 200

Raw upstream body: `{"code":3012,"msg":"request has been blocked due to unusual activity.","logid":"..."}`.

**Repro without magpie**

Took `dress()` and `startHeaders()` from the plugin (scratch copy, exported for the test) and posted straight to `START_BASE`, mutating only `system` in the dressed body:

| dressed body | result |
|---|---|
| 3 ZCode blocks (what `dress()` emits for a system-less request) | 200 |
| 4th block: empty / plain `x` / `x` + `cache_control` | 405 (each) |
| block1 appended to (agent text after `stableSections`) | 200 |
| block1 replaced with `x` | 405 |
| block2 replaced with `y`, or emptied | 200 |
| block2 dropped (2 blocks) | 200 |
| only block0 (1 block) | 405 |
| block0 appended to | 405 |

So: 2–3 system blocks; block0 must stay byte-identical; block1 must keep ZCode's stable prefix; block2 is free. A 4th block — exactly what `dress()` adds for every agent — is refused.

**Fix**

Append the agent's own system text to block2 instead of adding blocks:

```js
b.system = [
  cached(PROMPT.cliPrefix),
  cached(PROMPT.stableSections.join("\n\n")),
  cached(
    "\n\n" + [PROMPT.beforeEnvironment, environment(provider, model, place), PROMPT.afterEnvironment].join("\n\n") +
    (own.length ? "\n\n" + own.map((x) => x.text).join("\n\n") : "")
  ),
]
```

Verified with the same harness: `system: "x"`, system + tools, a 32 KB system, and a multi-turn request all answer 200. `system: "Always answer with the single word BANANA."` is followed (the model answers `BANANA`), so system authority survives the move.

`start.test.mjs` asserts the current layout (`...zcodeSystem(...), {text: "You are opencode, an agent."}, ...`) and needs updating with the fix.

**Related**

- yetone/magpie#425 — the original Start Plan 405, fixed by dressing request","comments":[],"title":"zcode: Start Plan answers 405/3012 when the agent's system prompt is added as a 4th block"}
